candidates.exact_span: It is proposed that the permit be reissued for a 5-year term following regulations promulgated at 40 CFR §122.46(a).
candidates.computation_change_reason: The proposed permit term bounds which monitoring schedule and permit-year conditions are in force during Federal FY2025; a different reading of the reissuance term or its effective dates could change which monitoring obligations are treated as applicable in that period.

candidates.exact_span: This is a renewal of an existing permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: As a renewal, prior-permit limits and monitoring conditions may carry forward or be compared under the more-stringent rule; interpreting whether FY2025 is governed by renewed, superseded, or transitional conditions could change applicable limits and monitoring requirements.

candidates.exact_span: Regulations contained in 40 CFR §122.44 require that NPDES permit limits are developed that meet the more stringent of either technology-based effluent limitation guidelines, numerical and/or narrative water quality standard-based effluent limits, or the previous permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This selection rule determines which enforceable limit governs when multiple bases exist; different interpretations of how to compare technology-based, water-quality-based, narrative, and previous-permit limits could change the numeric or narrative limit used for compliance comparison.

candidates.exact_span: Technology-based effluent limitations are established in the proposed draft permit for TSS.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This identifies TSS as having technology-based enforceable limits rather than report-only monitoring; a different reading of whether TSS limits are numeric, seasonal, or otherwise conditioned could change limit applicability and how missing TSS results are classified.

candidates.exact_span: Water quality-based effluent limitations are established in the proposed draft permit for pH and TRC.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This assigns pH and TRC to water-quality-based limits rather than technology-based or report-only monitoring; interpreting whether those limits are numeric, narrative, or conditionally applicable could change compliance comparisons and the semantics of missing pH or TRC evidence.

candidates.exact_span: Regulations promulgated at 40 CFR §122.44 (a) require technology-based effluent limitations to be placed in NPDES permits based on ELGs where applicable, on BPJ in the absence of guidelines, or on a combination of the two.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The ELG-versus-BPJ basis governs how technology-based limits are derived; if applicability of promulgated guidelines or use of BPJ is read differently, the resulting enforceable TSS limit and whether a numeric comparison is possible could change.

candidates.exact_span: In the absence of promulgated guidelines for the discharge, permit conditions may be established using BPJ procedures.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether this discharge is treated as lacking promulgated guidelines and therefore subject to BPJ affects the derivation of technology-based limits; that interpretation could change the enforceable numeric limit applied to TSS.

candidates.exact_span: BCT - Technology-based standard for the discharge from existing industrial point sources of conventional pollutants including BOD, TSS, fecal coliform, pH, and O&G.
candidates.computation_change_reason: BCT classifies pH and TSS as conventional pollutants under a technology-based framework, which can conflict with the separate statement that pH limits are water-quality-based; different readings of which standard controls pH (and whether TSS is strictly BCT-based) could change the selected enforceable limit.
